ops.title: SECURITY: codeidentity accepts injection entitlements — rejectInjectionEntitlements exists only in trust/
ops.description:
Found by the Phase-0 invariant census, **verified independently at `origin/main` = `1d55b2a`** before filing.

## The defect

`rejectInjectionEntitlements` exists in exactly one of the two peer-verification implementations:

```
ccx code grep "rejectInjectionEntitlements"
# 2 matches in 1 files
### trust/verify_darwin.go:328,334
```

`codeidentity/verify_darwin.go` has **zero matches**. So `codeidentity` accepts a peer signed with injection-enabling entitlements — `get-task-allow`, `allow-jit`, `disable-library-validation` and friends — which `trust` rejects.

This is not a dormant code path. `codeidentity` is the verifier on the **launchd install path**: `deployment/{activation,apply,core,uninstall}.go` and `service/keepalive.go` all verify through it. So the install/upgrade path applies a weaker signing policy than the socket-peer path.

The census notes this was verbatim blocker #4 from review `94eda3c` — it was found, fixed in `trust`, and never propagated to the fork.

## Why it happened — the pattern, not the instance

This is the second confirmed instance of *the same* failure mode. Commit `d09ed52` (the `ErrPeerGone` classification fix) had to apply the identical change to **both** copies to be correct. A fix landing in one copy and not the other is the structural hazard, and there is no compile-time or CI signal for it.

That makes this **task's fix and census KILL-6 the same decision** — see open question Q7: (a) delete the `codeidentity` verifier, keep its value types (`CodeIdentity`, `PolicyDigest`, both PUBLIC-API with 4 external callers each), and route every check through `trust`; or (b) port `rejectInjectionEntitlements` into `codeidentity` and keep both, which reopens the divergence. (a) is preferred; the deciding evidence is whether `trust.ProcessVerifier` is usable from `deployment`'s call sites, which verify an on-disk artifact rather than a live socket peer.

**Do not fix this by copying the function.** A same-fix-twice patch closes this instance and preserves the generator.

## Interim exposure

Until resolved, a binary signed with `allow-jit` passes `codeidentity` verification and can be installed and activated as a LaunchAgent by any daemonkit consumer using the deployment path.

ops.text: codeidentity and trust apply the same signing policy, proven by a shared table-driven test that feeds identical fixtures to both entry points and asserts identical verdicts — or codeidentity's verifier is deleted and every deployment/ and service/keepalive.go call site routes through trust
A test pins that a peer signed with allow-jit / get-task-allow / disable-library-validation is REJECTED on the launchd install path, not just the socket-peer path
The structural fix is chosen over the copy-the-function fix: either one implementation remains, or a single shared policy function is called by both and divergence is impossible by construction
